topic: Timber and wood: timber trees in Nepal, types and properties of wood

questions.q: 294. The artificial seasoning of timber may
questions.explain: Seasoning is the process of removing the sap or moisture from timber to prevent decay and improve its stability for construction.

questions.q: 295. Which one of the following does not belong to endogenous trees?
questions.explain: Endogenous trees grow inwards (like bamboo or palm). Teak is an exogenous tree, meaning it grows outwards by adding annual rings.

questions.q: 296. Which one of the following does not belong to exogenous trees?
questions.explain: Coconut is an endogenous tree; its fibers are distributed throughout the stem rather than growing in concentric rings.

questions.q: 297. The solution of salts from the soil absorbed by the trees which becomes a viscous solution due to loss of moisture and action of carbon dioxide is known as
questions.explain: As per Key b but Sap is the fluid that circulates through a plant's vascular system, carrying nutrients and water.

questions.q: 298. The age of tree can be judged from
questions.explain: In exogenous trees, one annual ring is typically added each year. Counting these rings in a cross-section reveals the tree's age.

questions.q: 299. The no. of annual ring in a log of 30 then life of the timber is
questions.explain: Since one annual ring generally represents one year of growth, 30 rings indicate a tree life of 30 years.

questions.q: 300. The layer between the bark of the tree and the sap wood which is not yet converted into wood is called
questions.explain: The cambium layer is the thin layer of living cells between the inner bark and the sapwood where new wood and bark cells are produced.

questions.q: 301. Which of the following is not a hard wood?
questions.explain: Deodar is a coniferous tree (softwood), whereas Sal, Teak, and Oak are deciduous (hardwood).

questions.q: 302. Which of the following is not a soft wood?
questions.explain: Sisham (Rosewood) is a dense hardwood. Deodar and Kail are common softwoods.

questions.q: 303. When the timber is attacked by fungus and reduced to powder, it is called
questions.explain: Dry rot is a form of decay caused by specific fungi that digest the cellulose of the wood, leaving it brittle and powdery.

questions.q: 304. In dry rot, wooden material defect caused due to
questions.explain: Dry rot is exclusively a fungal disease that spreads in timber with poor ventilation and moderate moisture.

questions.q: 305. Which of the following wood has the maximum resistance to white ants?
questions.explain: Teak contains natural oils and silica that make it highly resistant to termites (white ants) and decay.

questions.q: 306. Creosote oil is used to preserve the wood from
questions.explain: Creosote is a powerful wood preservative that prevents fungal rot and deters wood-boring insects and termites.

questions.q: 307. Timber can be made reasonably fire resistant
options: by soaking it in ammonium sulphate
by pumping creosote oil into timber under high pressure
questions.explain: Ammonium sulphate or borax are fire-retardant chemicals that release non-combustible gases when heated, protecting the timber.

questions.q: 308. The main purpose of seasoning is
options: to make the timber fire resistant
to remove the moisture from the timber at uniform rate
to make the timber water proof
questions.explain: Seasoning aims to reduce the moisture content (sap) of timber to equilibrium with the surroundings to prevent warping and shrinkage.

questions.q: 309. Which one is false?
options: seasoning is done to control moisture
sal wood is used for ornamental purpose
sap is suck in spring by roots of the tree
questions.explain: Sal wood is very hard and durable, making it excellent for structural beams and door frames, but it is too coarse for fine ornamental/furniture work.

questions.q: 310. The seasoning of timber
options: makes the timber light, strong and stable
prevents warping, cracking and shrinkage in timber
makes timber resistant to decay by fungi, termites etc.
questions.explain: Properly seasoned timber is more durable, easier to work with, and less prone to biological attacks or structural deformation.

questions.q: 311. Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: kiln seasoned timber is stronger than natural seasoned timber
moisture content in the timber can be reduced to any desired level in kiln seasoning
kiln seasoning is quicker than natural seasoning
kiln seasoning requires less stacking space but more expensive
questions.explain: Kiln seasoning is faster and more controlled, but it doesn't necessarily make timber 'stronger' than natural air seasoning; if done too fast, it can actually cause internal stress.

questions.q: 312. In a well-seasoned timber, the moisture content will be in the range of
questions.explain: For most construction purposes, timber is considered well-seasoned when its moisture content is reduced to roughly 10-12%.

questions.q: 313. Most economical methods of sawing wood is
questions.explain: Flat (or plain) sawing is the quickest and most economical method with minimal waste, although it is more prone to warping.

questions.q: 314. A thin sheet of wood sliced from a log of wood is called
questions.explain: Veneers are thin slices of wood, usually thinner than 3mm, used to cover cheaper wood surfaces or glued together to make plywood.

questions.q: 315. The number of veneers glued under pressure in a plywood must be
questions.explain: Plywood layers (plies) are always an odd number to ensure structural balance and prevent the board from warping or curling.

questions.q: 316. The curved swellings from the growth of layers or wounds left after branches are cut off in an irregular manners, are known as
questions.explain: Rind galls are curved swellings that form over a wound on the tree, often where a branch has been improperly removed.

questions.q: 317. The defects in wood due to hardening is
questions.explain: as per key c but The options listed (knots, rind galls, burls) are growth defects. Hardening usually refers to 'case hardening' during improper seasoning, which is not listed.

questions.q: 318. The defect caused by the shrinkage of timber is
questions.explain: A crook is a warp along the edge of a board, typically caused by uneven shrinkage during the drying process.

questions.q: 319. Knots in timber are
questions.explain: Knots are the bases of branches that have been encased by the subsequent growth of the wood in the main trunk.

questions.q: 320. Impregnating of timber is done to increase
questions.explain: Impregnating timber with chemicals (like Abel's process) is primarily done to improve its resistance to fire or biological decay.

questions.q: 321. Based on its dry weight, a freshly felled tree may contain water
questions.explain: Freshly cut timber (green timber) can often have a moisture content of 100% or more relative to its oven-dry weight.

questions.q: 322. The time required for the seasoning of timber in air is about
questions.explain: As per key c but While it varies by species and thickness, initial air seasoning of thin softwoods can take as little as 1 to 2 months to reach a workable state.

questions.q: 323. In the manufacture of ply woods the veneers are placed such that the grains of one layer are
options: at 45° with the grains of the other
at right angles with the grains of the other
at 60° with the grains of the other
parallel to the grains of the other
questions.explain: Cross-lamination (placing grains at 90°) gives plywood uniform strength in both directions and reduces shrinkage/expansion.

questions.q: 324. Plywood is identified by
questions.explain: Commercial plywood is primarily categorized and sold based on its thickness (e.g., 4mm, 6mm, 12mm).

questions.q: 325. Plywood is obtained by gluing wooden sheets at a specification of
questions.explain: The manufacture of plywood requires both high mechanical pressure and specific heat to cure the adhesive bonds between veneers.

questions.q: 326. Plywood is generally available
questions.explain: While available in many sizes, 3-ply boards typically start around the 3 to 4 mm thickness range.

questions.q: 327. Which has great strength against the rut?
questions.explain: Teak is renowned for its extreme durability and resistance to rot and fungal attacks due to its natural oils.

questions.q: 328. The wood of which tree is used to make cricket bat
questions.explain: Willow wood is used because it is incredibly light, tough, and has high shock resistance (impact energy absorption).

questions.q: 329. The seasoning of timber is done for
questions.explain: Seasoning involves controlling the drying process to reach an equilibrium moisture content relative to the surrounding humidity.

questions.q: 330. The strength of timber is maximum along
questions.explain: Timber is an anisotropic material; its tensile and compressive strength are significantly higher when loaded parallel to the fibers (grains).

questions.q: 331. Seasoning of timber is done to
options: reduce the weight of the timber
questions.explain: Removing moisture makes the timber lighter for transport, stable against further shrinkage, and less susceptible to rot.

questions.q: 332. The defects in the growth of timber are called
questions.explain: Shakes (separations between rings) and checks (cracks across rings) are common structural defects occurring during growth or seasoning.

questions.q: 333. The trunk of tree left after cutting all the branches is known as
questions.explain: A 'log' is the raw trunk of a tree that has been felled and delimbed but not yet sawn into lumber.

questions.q: 334. A piece of sawn timber whose c/s dimensions exceed 5 cm, in one direction and 20 cm in the other direction, is called a
questions.explain: A baulk is a roughly squared timber piece of large cross-section, usually exceeding 50mm in thickness and 200mm in width.

questions.q: 335. A piece of timber whose thickness and width are respectively 5 cm and 10 cm is called
questions.explain: A 'deal' is a specific commercial size of sawn softwood, typically between 5-10cm thick and 20-25cm wide.

questions.q: 336. The chemical used in preserving timber are
questions.explain: Zinc chloride, coal tar, and creosote are all well-known chemical preservatives used to protect wood from moisture and pests.

questions.q: 337. The trees yielding hard wood is
questions.explain: Shisham is a broad-leaved exogenous tree (hardwood). Chir, Deodar, and Pine are conifers (softwoods).

questions.q: 338. The trees yielding soft wood is
questions.explain: Chir and Deodar are conifers, which produce softwood. Sal, Teak, and Shisham are hardwoods.

questions.q: 339. According to IS:399-1963, the weight of the timber is specified at
questions.explain: Standard engineering codes usually specify timber properties and density at a standard moisture content of 12%.

questions.q: 340. Ply wood is made from
questions.explain: Plywood is typically manufactured using veneers from common available timbers like mango, teak, or pine, depending on the required grade.

questions.q: 341. The sports goods are made from
questions.explain: Mulberry is highly valued for sports goods (like hockey sticks) due to its toughness and flexibility.

questions.q: 342. The timber used for decorative wood work
questions.explain: As per key c but Shisham, Siris, and Rosewood all have beautiful grain patterns and colors, making them ideal for high-end furniture and decorative carving.

questions.q: 343. The unit weight of sal is
questions.explain: As per key c but Sal is a very dense and heavy hardwood, with a unit weight typically around 880 to 950 kg/m3.

questions.q: 344. Normally the wood used for scaffolding is
questions.explain: Bamboo is the standard for scaffolding due to its high strength-to-weight ratio, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness.

questions.q: 431. To prevent the attack of insects, the lower ends of the wooden posts that are to be embedded in ground are generally
questions.explain: Charring (scorching the surface) is an old method to protect timber from moisture and insects when buried in soil.

questions.q: 432. As assembled product made up of veneers and adhesives is called
questions.explain: The key specifies 'd' (plank), though technically a product made of veneers is Plywood. I am adhering to the key.
